text.p: The Andersons Inc said on Monday that the National Grain and Feed Association (NGFA) ordered Michigan farmer Horton Farms Inc to pay the company $211,400 in a dispute involving hedged-to-arrive contracts.
The NGFA decision also called for Horton to pay attorney fees and interest, the grain merchant said in a press release.

"This case may be particularly relevant to grain producers as it involves the so-called HTA grain contracts which have received considerable media attention in the past year," said Mike Anderson, president and chief operating officer of The Andersons.

Hedged-to-arrive contracts, a variant of the traditional way farmers sell grain to country elevators, allow farmers to set the "basis" or price spread to futures contracts at a date after the sale and before delivery, or to delay or "roll over" grain delivery.
Many farmers defaulted on delivery of HTAs and sought relief from the courts after last summer's record-breaking corn prices translated into heavy losses for those who used the contracts.

Andersons had as usual sold grain futures to "hedge" against lower prices, carrying the futures losses on their books until the grain was delivered. Under HTA's, farmers were liable for the losses once the grain was delivered.

Andersons said the specific case involved nine separate HTA contracts for the purchase of corn by Andersons from Horton and arose "as a result of Horton's failure to deliver grain against the contracts."
In its decision, an NGFA arbitration panel found that binding contracts existed and that Horton was "clearly in default," Andersons said.
